criterion.summary: Two-part: p_astro > 0.5 (the table criterion) and FAR below the GWTC-1 threshold of 1 per 30 days even after a trials factor of 5 banks. Both explicitly borrowed from GWTC-1. Sub-threshold = 0.1 < p_astro < 0.5.
criterion.quote: Also consistent with this is the fact that we find six new events with (a) false alarm rates below the threshold of 1 in 30 days defined in GWTC-1 (even after applying appropriate trials factors), and (b) probabilities of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro} > 0.5$, as effectively quantified by their consistency with the rates of occurrence of louder events. || The criterion in Table~\ref{tab:signalsFound} is based on the value of $p_{\rm astro}$, but all the events have significantly higher values of the `per-bank' IFAR than the threshold of 1 in 30 days, or $\sim 0.25$ O2, adopted in GWTC-1 \cite{LIGOScientific:2018mvr} (i.e., their IFARs exceed 0.25 O2 even if divided by a trials factor of five).
criterion.section: Sec. II 'Preview of results' (first sentence) and Sec. V 'Overview of the newly discovered BBH mergers' (second); Table II caption: 'New events with astrophysical probability $> 50\%$'

second_paper.section: Sec. I Introduction; Sec. II.C 'Determining the False-Alarm Rate'
second_paper.quote: The search described in this paper revealed two additional interesting BBH triggers that are above the thresholds of significance for being called events~\cite{LIGOScientific:2018mvr}. || If this trigger also has a high probability of being astrophysical in nature (see more details in Sec.~\ref{sec:PASTRO}), we can add it to the catalog of events [...]
second_paper.summary: No explicit p_astro threshold restated; relies on GWTC-1 thresholds of significance; FAR via L1-rank × FAP, p_astro computed (0.86, 0.68).

criterion.source_note: 1904.07214 uses \newcommand{\change}[2]{{#1}}, so the FIRST argument of \change{...}{...} is what renders; both quotes above are inside the first argument and therefore appear in this source's rendering.

tiers.name: new events, p_astro > 0.5 (Table II)
tiers.quote: Three of the mergers (GW170121, GW170304, GW170727) have inferred probabilities of being of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro} > 0.98$. The remaining three (GW170425, GW170202, GW170403) are less certain, with $p_{\rm astro}$ ranging from $0.5$ to $0.8$.

tiers.name: previously reported LVC events recovered (Table I)
tiers.quote: We detect all previously reported BBH events except for GW170608, for which the LVC did not provide the Hanford data in their bulk data release [...] All of these events are certainly astrophysical sources with lower limit on $p_{\rm astro} \geqslant 0.99$.
tiers.section: Sec. IV 'Results on the previously reported events', 1904.07214

tiers.name: sub-threshold candidates (Table III)
tiers.quote: we list in Table~\ref{tab:subthreshold candidates} the sub-threshold triggers of our search, defined as those with $0.1 < p_{\rm astro} < 0.5$.

tiers.name: single-detector-search new events (GW vs GWC prefix)
tiers.quote: We name the two new events GWC170402 and GW170817A according to the date of occurrence.

below_criterion.notes: GW170818 (LVC event) is not counted here; in 1904.07214 it lacks a p_astro and has per-bank FAR^-1 1.7 O2, see its event entry.

open_questions: GW170818: include as an IAS-O2 detection? 1904.07214 tabulates it among 'events already reported... as detected with our pipeline' but gives FAR^-1 1.7 O2 and no p_astro; 1910.09528 assigns IFAR > 1000 O2 and 'confirm[s] its astrophysical origin' but gives no p_astro.

GWC170402: paper counts it among 'two new events' and it has p_astro 0.68 > 0.5, but deliberately withholds the 'GW' prefix ('temporary GWC for GW candidate'; 'if genuine'). Decide whether it counts as a detection.
GW170425 inverse FAR: table says 15 O2, text says ≈ 29 O2.
GW170817A GPS: Table I 1186974184.716 vs Fig. 2 caption 1186974148.716 (transposition).
The 1910.09528 events have no IAS p_astro computed by the 1904.07214 rate-marginalised method; its p_astro uses a cruder volume-ratio argument (Q with order-unity uncertainty per the paper).

1904.07214 FARs are per-bank without trials factor; per-event GPS times are 'linear-free' template times in Hanford (for 1904.07214) and L1-trigger times (presumably) in 1910.09528 — the latter is not stated.
GW170121 appears in both papers with slightly different GPS (1169069154.565 in 1904.07214 vs 1169069154.564 in 1910.09528) and rho_L^2 (89.7 vs 90.8).
